terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation: the thing enjoyed is the subject (mē dēlectat), or the passive dēlector takes the ablative
evidence: Cic. Sen. 51: quibus ego incrēdibiliter dēlector
Cic. Att. 2.6.1: aut librīs mē dēlectō
terms.comment: Latin turns the sentence round: what one enjoys delights one (mē dēlectat, with an infinitive as subject: dēlectābat lūdere), or one is delighted by it (dēlector with the ablative). “Did you enjoy it?” is placuitne? (see what did you like best?).

terms.grammar: impersonal of juvō, with an infinitive or a thing as subject
evidence: Hor. S. 2.6.32: hoc juvat et mellī est

terms.gloss: enjoy (what one has: life, company, sleep)
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, deponent, with the ablative
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: the enjoyment of a thing, narrower than ūtī, “use” (see enjoy, have the benefit of).

terms.gloss: amuse; oblectāre sē, enjoy oneself, have a good time
evidence: Cic. Q. fr. 2.11.4: oblectā tē cum Cicerōne nostrō
Cic. Off. 3.58: ubi sē oblectāre … posset

phrases.latin: veniō nunc ad voluptātēs agricolārum, quibus ego incrēdibiliter dēlector
phrases.english: I come now to the pleasures of farmers, which I enjoy beyond belief
but what we enjoyed was playing

phrases.latin: oblectā tē cum Cicerōne nostrō quam bellissimē
phrases.english: have as lovely a time as you can with our little Cicero

phrases.latin: Sed etiam mē dēlectat basipilā lūdere.
phrases.english: But I also like to play baseball.
